note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Servers are started hidden by prepare (helper C:\lab\mgnet\svc.ps1) and their logs are shown with Get-Content/Select-String. Benchmarks and the load test must have the machine to themselves: plug in, power plan Best performance, nothing else running. Numbers on screen are the laptop's own. The BenchmarkDotNet host banner (CPU model, OS build) must be cropped; the prompt is neutral (PS>).
prepare: if (-not (Get-Command dotnet-counters -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { dotnet tool install -g dotnet-counters }

screens.app: Windows Terminal (two panes, played by Start-WtLayout.ps1)
setup: Action 'prepare: series/net/episodes/09-performance-optimization' (svc helper, dotnet-counters install, builds) once per session

Action 'screen-prepare: series/net/episodes/09-performance-optimization/counters': starts the API hidden on :5209 (fresh perf.db, cold cache), then a Windows Terminal window 'dotnet-counters | MG net09' / 'client | MG net09' whose panes wait for the take
Move the pointer off the window (other monitor)
steps: (take starts: window.json + window.go; the panes start when the recorder creates recordings\recording)

Nothing to click: left pane starts dotnet-counters monitor; right pane reads the summary once (fills the cache), eight more times, POSTs one request, waits 1.5 s and reads once more, then creates recordings\stop (about 30 s)
After the take: action 'screen-teardown: series/net/episodes/09-performance-optimization/counters' (closes the panes and dotnet-counters); the episode teardown stops the API
screens.expected: Left: [ProjectRequests.Perf] with mglab.perf.summary.computed ({computation} / 1 sec) and mglab.perf.requests.created ({request} / 1 sec) (they appear with the first read). summary.computed shows 1 for one interval after the first read, stays 0 during the eight reads, shows 1 again after the read that follows the POST; requests.created shows 1 after the POST. Right: the POST prints the created request as JSON (title Counter demo, budget 75000, FIN).
screens.note: dotnet-counters runs attached to the pane's console (#raw: no pipeline) so its live table renders; its output is not in the pane transcript. Counters are per-second rates: each tick shows as 1 for one refresh.
